standfirst: Three actresses, one woman, twenty years of appearance as a currency that ruins everybody who trades in it. Mask Girl is structured like a relay race, and each handover resets the genre. These six share its cruelty about status and its refusal to let anybody off.

picks.why: Revenge built over decades, executed coldly. Both start from a humiliation that a system declined to punish and follow the arithmetic all the way out. Both are also about what the pursuit does to the pursuer's face and body. Difference: The Glory keeps one protagonist and one moral position; Mask Girl swaps both, twice.

Women, money and the exact price of climbing. The same noir logic: a woman decides to want more than she was allotted, and the show tracks every favour that decision costs her. Difference: it is sisters against a dynasty rather than one woman against her own reflection, and it stays stylish where Mask Girl gets ugly.

Appearance as a ranking system. Both take the idea that being looked at is a form of violence and build a machine out of it, and both are strongest when the victim starts playing. Difference: a closed classroom setting and a 12 episode arc, so it is tighter and much less explicit.

Status as a game with rules you can read. The same black comic distance and the same willingness to make you complicit in watching somebody degrade themselves for money. Difference: it is a single allegorical space with no timeline, so nobody gets the twenty year consequence Mask Girl insists on.

Bleak Korean crime with no comfort offered. Both centre a woman whose interior life the show declines to explain, and both let dread do the work that plot usually does. Difference: The Frog withholds an answer entirely, where Mask Girl over-explains its final chapter.

Beauty and money as an enforcement mechanism. The surfaces are the point in both: a school that ranks by wealth and looks, shot like an advertisement, with a revenge plot underneath. Difference: Hierarchy styles the cruelty and stops there, while Mask Girl follows it to a prison and a daughter.

against.title: Celebrity
against.why: The other 2023 Netflix series about internet fame, and the pairing everybody makes. It sets up the same rot then softens into a whodunnit, and its heroine stays likeable, which is the one thing Mask Girl refuses to do.

against.title: Extracurricular
against.why: Paired for the moral bleakness. That show is about teenagers making one criminal decision under pressure; Mask Girl is about twenty years of adult self-loathing and its consequences for a child.

against.title: Squid Game
against.why: Named because it is Korean, on Netflix and violent. There is no game, no ensemble and no allegory here, just one face and what the world does to it.
